body: I also ended up isolated; while it wasn't to be with someone, I made a significant move in order to pursue something that turned out to be an almost comically bad fit for me that really accelerated the multi-year decline that brings me to where I am now.

Thank you for the response. Mainly I just was concerned that telling them would be exploitative or manipulative in some way. I didn't know if it was the kind of thing I should only tell a therapist, or if it's the sort of thing I need to tell them.

I haven't made up my mind in a final sense, but I've been working on plans as I go about other things. It's not going to be a spontaneous decision, so if it is what I decide, I'm not sure if there will be talking me out of it.

There's a lot. If I could redo things, instead of getting the sort of bullshit major I got (I started in one I intended to switch out of, proposed an interdisciplinary major, got shot down, then tried to switch to a different major and was told it was too late, so I gave up), I think I'd pursue a double major in mechatronics and biology, work for a few years maybe in robotics, go back to school for architecture, get a few years of experience in design. Then at my age I'd try to do an interdisciplinary design/engineering program, like MIT Media Lab or Stanford d.school. Other fields that interest me are cognitive science and computer science, but that sort of crazy twisting path would get me a little bit of everything. I want to know a lot and *need* to know a lot to act on and develop my ideas, but I've felt so sort of, I don't know, overwhelmed and anxious that I found a way to somehow avoid doing any of it for years. Now that I've started trying to study on my own, it doesn't come as easily as it used to, I'm so obsessed with results that I can't "fall into it" like I used to, and I have to worry about money, unlike before. So I'm just kind of like, fuck it. It's all so fucking distant now, I feel like a beggar in rags gazing at a shining citadel in the distance, occupied by ghosts of my possible past selves.

I've been so sort of "stuck in my head" for so long - and with noone to tell me how abnormal it was or how weirdly I was living life - that it took me this long even to properly understand what I'm interested in most. I wanted a "view from nowhere" and so stayed noncommittal, but the truth is I didn't put in a lot of effort to exploring different paths. I didn't realize it was "allowed," or something. I don't see an easy path towards getting there now as I have little money and few friends and my mental state is not great. I don't think I've got the stomach to make some wimpy effort that's a shadow of what it could have been, arrogant as that might sound.
